## Grip Strength Test Analysis

-- **Illustration:**  
Boxplots and individual scores  

```{r gs_data_loading}

#here we clear the working directory again in case the script is used as a child
rm(list = ls())

#--------------------------- 1. Manual Entries -----------------------------#
# 1.1 INPUT FILES
file_path <- "~/AOCF-Behavioral Tests/Grip Strength test/validation/group data/"

raw_data_file <- "Grip_strength_group data_results_ns.xlsx"

#---------------------------2. LOAD DATA-----------------------------#
# Load data
raw_data <- read_excel(paste(file_path,raw_data_file,sep = ""))
raw_data <- na.omit(raw_data)

# Factor the genotype/group/sex variable 
data <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(gender = as.factor(sex),
         group = as.factor(group))  

```

### Experimental conditions

4 groups of mice:

-> all data can be used

The analysis of the data is done in this Rmd file directly.

### Results

#### Average Grip Strength

```{r pl_lat, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 9}

#---------------------------3. ANALYSIS-----------------------------#
# 3.1 Grip Strength Test
# 3.1.1 Average Grip Strength

pl_strength <- data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = Average, color = group, label ="")) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  #add data-points (not overlapping)
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.75), size = 2) +
  #define position of 'n='
  stat_n_text(y.pos = 5) +
  #axis title
  labs(x="", 
       y = "Average (lbf)",  
       title = "Average grip strength in pound-force") +
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() + 
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

#pl_strength  

pl_strength_s <- data %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = Average, color = sex, label ="")) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NULL) +
  #add data-points (not overlapping)
  geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(dodge.width = 0.75), size = 2) +
  #define position of 'n='
  stat_n_text(y.pos = 5) +
  #count n of each gender and add it to the plot  
  geom_text(aes(label=after_stat(count), y = after_stat(count)), stat="count", position = position_dodge(width = 0.95), size=4) + 
  
#  geom_text(aes(label=..count.., y = ..count..), stat="count", position = position_dodge(width = 0.95), size=4) +
  #axis title
  labs(x="", 
       y = "Average (lbf)",  
       title = "Average grip strength in pound-force") +
  #add a theme
  theme_pubr() +
  #legend
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(vjust= 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 12))

#pl_strength_s
  
#arrange the 2 plots created above into a grid with 1 rows and 2 column with automatic labelling (A,B)
Fig1 <- ggarrange(pl_strength, pl_strength_s, labels="AUTO", ncol=1, nrow=2, common.legend=F, legend = "bottom")

Fig1

```

__Figure 1.__ Comparison of average grip strength in pound-force (lbf) between groups (A) and between gender within group (B). 

\newpage

__Statistics for Figure 1 A.__

```{r fig1a stats}

# Stats for Figure 1 (COMPARISON BETWEEN GROUPS)
#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

stat_data <- pl_strength$data

# perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare within genotpye difference
st = tidy(pairwise.wilcox.test(stat_data$Average, stat_data$group, exact = FALSE, p.adjust.methods="BH")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",
          variable = "Fig 1 A, average grip strength (lbf)",
          test = paste("between groups"), 
          sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", ""))

#combine stats from every iteration of the loop
stats = bind_rows(stats, st)

#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
#  kable_styling(latex_options="scale_down") 
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position=TRUE","scale_down"))  
#  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down"))

```

__Statistics for Figure 1 B. (Between genders)__

```{r fig1b1 stats}

# Stats for Figure 1 (COMPARISON BETWEEN GENDERS)
# list of gender
list_of_genders <- as.factor(c("f", "m"))

# list of groups
list_of_groups <- c("1", "2", "3", "4")

#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

for (i in 1:length(list_of_groups)) {
  stat_data <- pl_strength_s$data %>%
    filter(group == list_of_groups[i])
    # perform Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare within group difference
 st = tidy(wilcox.test(stat_data$Average ~ stat_data$sex, exact = FALSE)) %>%
    mutate(method = "Wilcoxon Sum",
          variable = "Fig 1 B, average grip strength (lbf)",
          test = paste("between genders in group", list_of_groups[i]), 
          sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
  #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
 }

#format the table
stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
#  kable_styling(latex_options="scale_down")   
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position=TRUE","scale_down"))
#  kable_styling(latex_options = c("hold_position","scale_down"))

```

__Statistics for Figure 1 B. (Between groups)__

```{r fig1b2 stats, tbl-pos: H}

# Stats for Figure 1 (COMPARISON BETWEEN GROUPS)
#create a tibble to collect all stats
stats = tibble()

for (i in 1:length(list_of_genders)) {
  stat_data <- pl_strength_s$data %>%
    filter(sex == list_of_genders[i])
  # perform Pairwise Wilcoxon Rank Sum Tests to compare between group difference
  st = tidy(pairwise.wilcox.test(stat_data$Average, stat_data$group, exact = FALSE, p.adjust.methods="BH")) %>%
    mutate(method = "Pairwise Wilcoxon Sum",
          variable = "Fig 1 B, average grip strength (lbf)",
          test = paste("between groups for", list_of_genders[i]), 
          sign=ifelse(p.value < 0.05, "*", "")) #%>%
  #combine stats from every iteration of the loop
  stats = bind_rows(stats, st)
 }

stats%>%
  #remove horizontal lines between rows
  kable(booktabs = T) %>%
  #prevent table from floating and scale it to page-width
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("HOLD_position=TRUE","scale_down"))

```
